2607.04814.title: Evaluating the Effect of Linguistic Relatedness on Cross-Lingual Transfer in Large Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
2607.04814.paper_summary: Extending automatic speech recognition (ASR) to low-resource African languages is constrained by the prohibitive demands of data collection at scale. A promising direction is to leverage linguistic relatedness to enhance cross-lingual transfer from a related auxiliary language to the low-resource target by sequentially adapting on both. Although this strategy has shown meaningful improvements in small ASR models, its effectiveness in large ASR remains unclear. We extend this framework to large multilingual ASR through a systematic controlled experimental design spanning six factors, two Africa-centric corpora, and four large ASR models, isolating whether linguistic relatedness reliably predicts cross-lingual transfer gains in this setting. Across all conditions, pre-adaptation on related auxiliary languages yields no practically meaningful transfer improvements given minimal target-language data, suggesting that linguistic relatedness alone may not reliably predict cross-lingual transfer gains in large multilingual ASR, or constitute an effective strategy for extending such models to low-resource languages.
2607.04814.paper_summary_zh: 擴展自動語音識別（ASR）到低資源的非洲語言受到大規模數據收集的高昂需求的限制。一個有前景的方向是利用語言相關性來增強從相關輔助語言到低資源目標語言的跨語言轉移，通過對兩者進行逐步適應。儘管這一策略在小型 ASR 模型中顯示出有意義的改進，但其在大型 ASR 中的有效性仍不清楚。我們通過一個系統的控制實驗設計將這一框架擴展到大型多語言 ASR，涵蓋六個因素、兩個以非洲為中心的語料庫和四個大型 ASR 模型，隔離語言相關性是否可靠地預測在此情境下的跨語言轉移增益。在所有條件下，對相關輔助語言的預適應在目標語言數據極少的情況下未能產生實質上有意義的轉移改進，這表明僅僅依賴語言相關性可能無法可靠地預測大型多語言 ASR 中的跨語言轉移增益，或構成將此類模型擴展到低資源語言的有效策略。
